findings.title: Screenshot harness reports a failed page as an 'ok' shot
findings.claim: If `main()` in `.art/shots/main.ts` throws (for example 'no contact window to aim at'), the catch writes the stack into the body and sets `shotReady = true` without logging to the console. `shot.cjs` then captures a page of error text, exits 0, and `all.mjs` prints `ok` because the PNG is over 1000 bytes. The `grep -v wrote shot.log` check stays silent too, since nothing at console level 3 or above was logged.
findings.evidence: plan L2169 (`main().catch((e) => { document.body.textContent = ...; shotReady = true; })`), L2206 (only console-message level >= 3 is logged), L2246 (`ok = r.status === 0 && existsSync(out) && statSync(out).size > 1000`), L2278 (the expected result is 'no page:, failed or uncaught lines').
findings.why: Step 4's machine check can pass on a broken harness. Only Step 5's manual look at each PNG would catch it.
findings.fix: In the catch, also call `console.error(String(e?.stack ?? e))` and set `window.shotFailed = true`. In shot.cjs, read `window.shotFailed === true` after the ready loop, and if it is set, log `failed page` and `app.exit(1)`.

findings.title: The single player keyboard intercept wiring is untested
findings.claim: Task 7 passes `{ intercept: (code) => contact.intercept(code) }` to `createDuelKeyboard` in duelMode.ts, but no test checks it. The only new single player test is the duelModeDispose one, and that file's input mock ignores createDuelKeyboard's arguments. Online, the same wiring is covered by the new onlineDuelSession Escape tests.
findings.evidence: plan L1615 (the duelMode intercept), L1450-L1462 (the new duelModeDispose test only checks setContact); tests/duelModeDispose.test.ts:L8-L10 (`createDuelKeyboard: () => ({ ... })` drops its options).
findings.why: If the intercept were dropped or miswired in startDuelMode, every test would still pass, while Esc with the window open would pause the solo duel. That breaks spec §3's 'Esc and the pause' rule in single player.
findings.fix: Make the input mock in duelModeDispose.test.ts record its options, e.g. `createDuelKeyboard: (_t, o) => { h.kbOpts = o; return {...}; }`. Then, in the new test, take the controller handed to setContact, call `sync` with shown true at Weapons and `click(1)`, and assert `h.kbOpts.intercept('Escape') === true` and that the controller state is now null.

findings.title: `?mode=duel` gets the window, against the wording of spec §6.5
findings.claim: Spec §6.5 says that without the contact option 'nothing changes, which keeps ?mode=duel and the tests' scenes as they are'. The plan gives startDuelMode a controller in every case and also wires `setContact` in main.ts's `startDuel`, so `?mode=duel` shows the window. The plan states this under 'Resolved ambiguities' but does not explain the conflict with the spec sentence.
findings.evidence: spec L183; plan L1612-L1617 (startDuelMode always creates and passes the controller), L1754 (main.ts:186 `startDuel` gains setContact), L2323 ('`?mode=duel` also gets the window').
findings.why: This is a stated but unjustified deviation. It is harmless (a dev path), but the spec and the plan disagree on the record.
findings.fix: Add one line to the plan's deviation note explaining it: `?mode=duel` is the same solo duel and should match Single player. Or amend spec §6.5 to say that only the scene tests keep running without the option.
